quotes.author: William Shakespeare
quotes.quoteText: All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players.

quotes.author: Jane Austen
quotes.quoteText: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.

quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.quoteText: The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation.

quotes.author: Mark Twain
quotes.quoteText: Courage is resistance to fear, mastery of fear—not absence of fear.

quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.quoteText: A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds, adored by little statesmen and philosophers and divines.

quotes.author: Lewis Carroll
quotes.quoteText: Why, sometimes I've believed as many as six impossible things before breakfast.

quotes.author: Charles Dickens
quotes.quoteText: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity, it was the season of Light, it was the season of Darkness, it was the spring of hope, it was the winter of despair.

quotes.author: Emily Dickinson
quotes.quoteText: Tell all the truth but tell it slant — Success in Circuit lies.
quotes.source: Tell all the truth but tell it slant

quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.quoteText: The truth is rarely pure and never simple.

quotes.author: William Shakespeare
quotes.quoteText: The course of true love never did run smooth.

quotes.author: Herman Melville
quotes.quoteText: Call me Ishmael.

quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.quoteText: Early to bed and early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise.

quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.quoteText: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived.

quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.quoteText: There is only one thing in the world worse than being talked about, and that is not being talked about.

quotes.author: Walt Whitman
quotes.quoteText: Do I contradict myself? Very well then I contradict myself, (I am large, I contain multitudes.)

quotes.author: Mark Twain
quotes.quoteText: All right, then, I'll go to hell.

quotes.author: Emily Brontë
quotes.quoteText: Whatever our souls are made of, his and mine are the same.

quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.quoteText: In the woods, we return to reason and faith.

quotes.author: Jane Austen
quotes.quoteText: Silly things do cease to be silly if they are done by sensible people in an impudent way.

quotes.author: William Shakespeare
quotes.quoteText: Cowards die many times before their deaths; the valiant never taste of death but once.

quotes.author: Mark Twain
quotes.quoteText: Truth is stranger than fiction, but it is because Fiction is obliged to stick to possibilities; Truth isn't.

quotes.author: Charlotte Brontë
quotes.quoteText: I am no bird; and no net ensnares me: I am a free human being with an independent will.

quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.quoteText: We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.

quotes.author: Lewis Carroll
quotes.quoteText: Begin at the beginning, and go on till you come to the end: then stop.

quotes.author: Walt Whitman
quotes.quoteText: I believe a leaf of grass is no less than the journey-work of the stars.

quotes.author: Jane Austen
quotes.quoteText: You pierce my soul. I am half agony, half hope.

quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.quoteText: In this world nothing can be said to be certain, except death and taxes.

quotes.author: William Shakespeare
quotes.quoteText: This above all: to thine own self be true.

quotes.author: Emily Dickinson
quotes.quoteText: “Hope” is the thing with feathers — that perches in the soul.

quotes.author: Mark Twain
quotes.quoteText: Few things are harder to put up with than the annoyance of a good example.

quotes.author: Jane Austen
quotes.quoteText: The person, be it gentleman or lady, who has not pleasure in a good novel, must be intolerably stupid.

quotes.author: Charles Dickens
quotes.quoteText: Heaven knows we need never be ashamed of our tears, for they are rain upon the blinding dust of earth, overlying our hard hearts.
